question: A trader allows a discount of 10% on the marked price and still gains 8% on the whole. At what percentage above the cost price does he mark his goods?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**If Discount % and Profit % of a person is given,

Then we can directly use the formula,

(100 - D%)/(100 + P%) = CP/MP

Where,

D% = Discount %

P% = Profit %

From the above formula we can directly find out the ratio between MP and CP

(100 - 10)/(100 + 8) = CP/MP

⇒ 90/108 = CP/MP

⇒ CP/MP = 5/6

⇒ Markup % = (6 - 5)/5 × 100

⇒ Markup % = 20%

∴ The trader marks his goods 20% above the cost price.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 10%

Profit = 8%

**Formula used:**

Markup % = (MP - CP)/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Let Mark Price (MP) be 100

Selling price (SP) = 0.9 × 100 = 90 

Cost price × 1.08 = 90

⇒ Cost price (CP) = 250/3

Markup % = (MP - CP)/CP × 100

Markup % = (100 - frac{250)/(3)}{250/3} × 100

Markup % = 20%

**∴ The trader marks his goods 20% above the cost price.**
